activity: Activity 1.2 - Try It Yourself: Healthcare Management System

domains.reason: A patient profile contains nested and evolving information such as demographics, allergies, contacts, and care preferences. A JSON document keeps related profile fields together.

domains.family: Key-value store (Redis) for short-lived availability/cache data; a transactional database should remain the source of truth
domains.reason: Fast key-based reads can show available appointment slots and temporarily hold a slot during booking. Final booking confirmation needs transactional consistency in the authoritative scheduling system.
Large volumes of timestamped observations can be written continuously and queried by patient/device and time window when partition keys are designed for those access patterns.
A graph can efficiently traverse relationships among patients, clinicians, departments, referrals, and care networks.

domains.family: Object storage (Amazon S3; key-addressed object model)
domains.reason: Large files such as scans and reports are durable binary objects retrieved by object key, while metadata can be stored separately in a document database.

summary: A healthcare platform is polyglot: use each NoSQL family for the access pattern it handles best, while applying strict access control, encryption, auditing, retention rules, and appropriate clinical governance to sensitive records.
